text:
The trade that sent Matthew Knies to Columbus for Kirill Marchenko came together on the eve of opening night, and his first 17 games as a Blue Jacket have looked like a player still finding his footing. He has 3 goals and 8 points while playing 18:26 a night, a long way from the 23 goals and 66 points he put up in Toronto last season.

The slow start is part real, part bad bounces. His own chances are thinner than they were with the Leafs (0.69 expected goals per 60, down from 0.94), and Columbus has been outshot on quality with him at five on five (46% of expected goals). But his linemates have also finished about three goals below what those chances deserved, and over his last ten games he has 4 points where our numbers expected about 7.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says 56% of his shots came off the rush last season, so watch how often Columbus lets him attack in transition. His scoring rate sits well under our range for him, and that gap usually closes.
